test_cases.name: zevari_today_is_level_0
test_cases.input: Run the production architecture audit on Zevar i as described in the ladder. Today is raw SQL against any table.
assertions: Places the system at Level 0 No boundary
Names Level 1 as the floor and Level 2 modular monolith as the gold standard
Does not recommend microservices as the next step
Lists the three adoption changes: domain grouping, mechanical lint rule, expand/contract

test_cases.name: scorecard_uses_six_pillars
test_cases.input: Score this design against the production-grade architecture audit PDF.
assertions: Scores all six pillars: SoC, data modeling, state, APIs, migrations, scalability
Each pillar is out of 15 with target >= 12
Evidence notes cite criteria rather than inventing new pillars

test_cases.name: hexagonal_is_not_a_rung
test_cases.input: Should we add a hexagonal/DDD level between the modular monolith and microservices?
assertions: Says clean/hexagonal architecture and DDD are not separate rungs
Says they describe how to build level 2 well
Keeps the lead module as a hexagonal port inside level 2

test_cases.name: payback_is_level_1_boundary_gap
test_cases.input: Run the production architecture audit on Payback.ai. The Worker mounts routes per lane and has a contracts package, but routes/ledger.ts and routes/review.ts run SQL inline, and routes/eval.ts dedupes with an in-memory Map.
assertions: Places Payback.ai at Level 1 with Level 2 modular monolith as the gold standard
Names the inline SQL in route modules as the level-1 artefact and the one mechanical rule that fixes it
Scores all six pillars out of 15 and the total out of 90
